selectionReason: The remaining frozen rows at least one of whose KANJIDIC2 readings is used by an existing word article that declares the kanji, the rule announced on issue 60 after batch 136. At the base, coverage.py found 12 such rows with a declaring article: 鼓 (太鼓) aligned, and 11 marked as not aligned. Five of those 11 were misclassified, because the lean alignment had no readings for 怯, 贅, 椒 and 無, which have no cards and are outside the N1 set. With KANJIDIC2's 怯 キョウ, 贅 ゼイ, 椒 ショウ and 無 ム/ブ, the articles 卑怯 ひきょう, 贅沢 ぜいたく, 胡椒 こしょう, 無沙汰 ぶさた and 御無沙汰 ごぶさた use 卑 ヒ, 沢 タク, 胡 コ, 沙 サ and 汰 タ, and the pinned JMdict marks none of these spellings as ateji and none of the readings as gikun. This corrects the batch 149 selection reason, which set 胡 aside because 胡椒 used none of its KANJIDIC2 readings; こしょう uses コ. The batch is therefore 卑, 汰, 沙, 沢, 胡 and 鼓 in source-row order. No word article is added: six existing articles each change in one line, which gains eight links in all, and the same line of 無沙汰 replaces "None of these written characters has a card yet" with "無 does not have a card yet". No existing kanji card changes. A card quizzes each reading that a declaring word article uses, unless the pinned JMdict marks the spelling as ateji or the reading as gikun; all six quiz only their on reading, and every quizzed kun list is empty. The other six rows marked as not aligned (伯 戯 撲 皇 眼 邪) and 644 rows with no declaring article remain; from batch 156 the proposal on issue 60 governs the selection.

review.execution: All four runs started after the previous one ended. The two initial runs and confirm-gpt had at most one tool call in flight. confirm-claude once issued two read-only calls at once, at 09:00:29 UTC: two view calls of its packet's evidence/exclusion-proofs.md, for lines 1-50 and 50-140; its report says that every response contained exactly one tool call, which is inaccurate on this point. The final message of initial-claude is not identical to its saved report but contains it (similarity 0.98); the closure keeps the saved report. The initial-gpt audit flags one recursive shell command over the packet folder and counts it as a corpus scan; this is a false positive: the pattern matched ** in Python exponentiation and in a quoted Markdown string, in a script that compared the stroke files with their KanjiVG SVGs and opened named files only. The confirm-gpt audit flags one path outside the allowed folders, the parent review-packets folder that its shell commands used as a base path; this is also a false positive: every path built on it lies in the confirmation packet, the original packet or its family's initial report. Each confirmation was a fresh agent of the same model family, given the author's statement on its family's initial report and allowed to read the original packet and that report. Both families confirmed the same final commit 25609582, which was written (08:40:36 UTC) before either confirmation started.
